# University of the Andes (Colombia) – Summary
The University of the Andes (Uniandes), founded in 1948 in Bogotá, is Colombia's first nonsectarian and politically neutral university. Established to modernize higher education and supply skilled professionals required for national development, Uniandes became legally recognized as a university in 1964. Its governing structure consists of a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, Rector, Vice-Rectors, Deans, Faculty Councils, and support officers, with 14 academic units—including 10 faculties and several inter-disciplinary centers. The institution emphasizes academic excellence, ethical formation, pluralism, and social responsibility according to its Statutes.
The university's campus, situated in Bogotá's historical center, spans approximately 180,551 square meters and includes restored historic buildings, modern facilities, 219 laboratories, a central library and five satellites housing over 445,000 books, and extensive computing resources. Uniandes supports a diverse student body (55% male, 45% female, 30% from outside Bogotá) and provides interdisciplinary study opportunities, robust exchange programs with over 119 universities worldwide, and specialized support for international students. The mascot, Seneca the goat, symbolizes school tradition. The university boasts numerous prominent alumni in government, arts, science, and academia.
